title: Incident Relay Strip & After-Action Dossier — compact console surface for alerts/SLO context
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Goal: Design a compact, persistent "relay strip" for the Redwood Console incident stream that surfaces actionable context (SLO deltas, runbook links, quick responder notes) and a lightweight After-Action Dossier (AAD) that collects links and timeline snippets for fast post-incident wrap-up. The surface should reduce context switching for on-call engineers, surface cost signal and rollback recommendations for rollouts, and make it trivial to attach external postmortem artifacts (Confluence, Drive, GitHub) without leaving the console.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha V: Initial sketches uploaded; focused on three micro-actions: add runbook, attach artifact, create quick note. Asked Eng to validate feasibility of persistent socket for realtime SLO delta updates.
2026-03-04 — Marisol O (PM): Liked the AAD compact mode, requested explicit permission checks when surfacing private Drive links. Asked to show cost impact summary when rollout is implicated.

2026-03-06 — Nate L (Eng): Feasibility note: we can stream SLO deltas via existing metrics bus but need a lightweight aggregation layer to avoid noisy updates. Suggested limiting tokenized history to last 6 entries to keep KV cache usage predictable.
2026-03-08 — Jonah B: Prototype iteration 2 pushed to Figma; added affordance for 'mark for postmortem' and a small timeline scrubber. Flagged animation budget for mobile.
2026-03-09 — Accessibility review (Eve H): Ensure strip color semantics do not rely on color only; added high-contrast variant and keyboard-first focus order.
design_decisions: Decision 1: Use a dense horizontal strip pinned to the top of the incident detail panel (not global topbar) to avoid global chrome changes.
Decision 2: AAD will be a slide-over sheet anchored to the strip; sheet persists a curated list of links, short timeline snippets, and a 3-line editable incident summary.
Decision 3: SLO delta indicator shows relative % change + one-line blurb (e.g., "p99 latency +12% vs baseline"). Clicking opens the SLO detail modal.
Decision 4: Attachments are tokenized links with permission badge; we will surface 'private' marker and require a click-through modal to verify access before embedding content.
Decision 5: To balance telemetry cost, strip updates are rate-limited to 1 update / 15s per incident and additional low-priority diffs will be collapsed into a condensed summary.

Decision 6: Rollout-aware CTA: when an in-progress rollout is linked to the incident, surface a single 'rollback suggestion' CTA that opens the rollout timeline in a new tab rather than performing inline actions.
Decision 7: Keyboard-first interactions: map primary actions to mnemonic keys (r = runbook, a = attach artifact, n = note).
